data.title: Mastering Joint Probability in Two-Way Tables
data.description: Practice calculating the joint probability of two events occurring together using data from various contingency tables.

challenges.question: What is P(Under 30 AND Brand B)? Enter your answer as a decimal between 0 and 1 (round to 2 decimals).
challenges.hint: Find the cell where Under 30 and Brand B meet (18). Divide by the grand total (120).

challenges.question: What is P(Female AND Math)? Enter your answer as a decimal between 0 and 1 (round to 2 decimals).
challenges.hint: Find the cell where Female and Math meet (16). Divide by the grand total (80).

challenges.question: What is P(Under 1 mile AND Bus)? Enter your answer as a decimal between 0 and 1 (round to 2 decimals).
challenges.hint: Find the cell where Under 1 mile and Bus meet (5). Divide by the grand total (100).

challenges.question: What is P(Weekend AND Eats)? Enter your answer as a decimal between 0 and 1 (round to 2 decimals).
challenges.hint: Find the cell where Weekend and Eats meet (50). Divide by the grand total (120).

data.educationalContext: Joint probabilities help us understand the likelihood of multiple conditions being met at the same time, which is a fundamental concept in data analysis and statistics.
